nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿طسۤمۤ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: "طسۤمۤ" is a name.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ﴾.
Because the Qurʾān is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.
So the meaning is: these are "those verses of the Book".
And it was said: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ has the meaning of "these" (هذه).

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: i.e. killing.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. killing yourself out of eagerness for them.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿بَاخِعٌ﴾ i.e. destroying.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is from بَخَعَه, i.e. he humbled him.
And the meaning is: perhaps you will kill yourself because of their abandoning faith.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ آيَةً﴾.
i.e. had We willed, We would have compelled them to obedience by destroying everyone who disobeyed.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾.
There are several statements on this:
Mujāhid said: ﴿أعناقهم﴾: their great ones (chiefs).
Abū Zayd and al-Akhfash said: ﴿أعْنَاقُهُمْ﴾: their groups; one says: جاءني عُنُقٌ من النَّاس, i.e. a group (of people) came to me.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: ﴿خَاضِعِينَ﴾ and "خاضعةً" are one and the same here.
And al-Kisāʾī holds that the meaning is: (they remained) humbled toward it [Translator's note: the source reads خاضعيها].
Abū Jaʿfar said: Mujāhid's statement that ﴿أَعْنَاقُهُمْ﴾ are their great ones is [well known] in the language: one says جاءني عُنُقٌ من النَّاس, i.e. their chiefs; and likewise one says جاءني عُنُقٌ من الناس, i.e. a group. For this reason one says: "على فلانٍ عتْقُ رقبةٍ" (so-and-so must free a slave, lit. a neck [raqaba]), and one does not say "عَتْقُ عُنُقٍ", because of the ambiguity that occurs in it.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar's statement is the best of these statements, and it is the choice of Abū al-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad).
The meaning according to his statement is: so they remained humbled toward it. He gave the predicate about the muḍāf ilayhi, and brought the muḍāf as an inserted word (muqḥam) for emphasis, as the poet said:
رَأَتْ مَرَّ السِّنينَ أَخَذْنَ مِنّي * كَمَا أَخَذَ السِّرَارُ منَ الهِلاَلِ
(She saw the passing of the years [lit. "the passing" treated as plural] taking from me, as the last nights of the month take from the crescent.)
And as the poet said:
وتَشْرَقُ بالقَوْل الَّذي قَدْ أَذَعْتَهُ * كما شَرِقَتْ صَدْرُ القَناَةِ مِنَ الدَّمِ
(And you choke on the word that you have spread, as the head of the spear choked [feminine verb] with blood.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: And like it is: سقطتْ بعضُ أصابعه (some of his fingers fell [feminine verb]).
He said: And like it is:
يا تَيْمُ تَيْمَ عَدِيٍّ لا أَبَا لَكُمُ * لا يُلْقِيَنَّكُمُ في سَوْءَةٍ عُمَرُ
(O Taym, Taym of ʿAdī — may you have no father! — let not ʿUmar cast you into disgrace.)
So he brought the first "تَيْمَ" as inserted (muqḥam) for emphasis.
As for al-Kisāʾī's statement, it is an error according to the Basrans and al-Farrāʾ.
And such an omission does not occur anywhere in speech.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Of the plants of the earth, of what people and cattle eat.
It is narrated from al-Shaʿbī that he said: People are of the plants of the earth; whoever of them goes to Paradise is noble (karīm), and whoever goes to the Fire is base.
The meaning according to Mujāhid's statement is: of every beneficial, good kind.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً﴾.
i.e. an indication of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that there is nothing like Him.
Then He said ﴿وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. Allah knew that they would not believe, as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ، وَلا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
i.e. and recite this to them.
And after it: ﴿وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ. وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلاَ يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي﴾.
Al-Aʿraj, Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read ﴿ويَضِيقَ صَدْرِي. وَلاَ يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with يَضِيقَ in the accusative, conjoined to يُكَذِّبُونِ].
The first reading is better, because the (non-)loosening of the tongue is not among what falls under the fear, since it had already happened.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said ﴿فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَارُونَ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
The meaning is: so send to Hārūn so that he may help me and support me, as you say: "Send to me, for I will help you."

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: It means the killing of the soul. ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ i.e. because of my killing a man of theirs.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿قَالَ كَلاَّ فَٱذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُّسْتَمِعُونَ﴾.
﴿كَلاَّ﴾ is a deterrent and a rebuke, i.e. desist from this fear and trust in Allah.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿فَٱذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُّسْتَمِعُونَ﴾.
It is possible that ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ refers to Mūsā and Hārūn, peace be upon them both, because two are a plural, as He, the Exalted, said ﴿فَإنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾.
It is possible that it refers to Mūsā and Hārūn and the signs.
And it is possible that it refers to Mūsā and Hārūn and those to whom they were sent.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first is the most fitting of them, so that the meaning is: We are with you, helping and strengthening.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولاۤ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿رسولُ﴾ has the meaning of "message" (risāla), and he recited:
لَقَدْ كَذَب الوَاشُوْنَ مَا فُهْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ * بِسِرٍّ وَلا أَرْسَلتُهم برسُوْلِ
(The slanderers have lied: I did not utter a secret in their presence, nor did I send them a message [rasūl].)
The implied form according to his statement is: we are the bearers of a message.
And al-Akhfash holds that it is a singular that indicates two and a plural.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
The meaning is: He sent us so that you send the Children of Israel with us.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيداً﴾.
i.e. a newborn; so he reminded him of his favour in raising him from when he was small until he grew up.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ﴾.
And (it may also be) مِن عُمْرِك and عَمْرِك.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِي فَعَلْتَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It means the killing of the soul.
Al-Shaʿbī read: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ﴾ with kasra on the fāʾ [i.e. فِعْلَتَك]; and fatḥa is for the first (reading), because it is for the single occurrence.
And kasra has the meaning of manner and state, i.e. your deed that is known, as he said:
كأنَّ مِشْيتَها مِنْ دَارِ جَارَتِهَا * مرُّ السَّحَابَةِ لا رَيْثٌ وَلا عَجَلُ
(As though her gait [mishya] from her neighbour's house were the passing of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty.)
And one says: that was in the days of al-radda and al-ridda (the apostasy).
Abū Jaʿfar said: "ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān" said — and he preferred that — since the apostasy occurred only once, fatḥa is better.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
There are several statements about its meaning:
a- Among them that the meaning is: (you are) of those ungrateful for my favour, as he said:
"والكُفْرُ مَخْبَثَةٌ لِنَفْسِ المُنْعِمِ"
(and ingratitude is a cause of disgust to the soul of the benefactor)
b- Al-Ḍaḥḥāk holds that the meaning is: and you are of the disbelievers because of your killing the Copt.
He said: So he denied disbelief of himself, and stated that he did that out of ignorance.
c- Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is: and you are now of the disbelievers.
d- Al-Suddī said: i.e. and you are of the disbelievers, because you used to follow us in the religion that you now find fault with; so you were of the disbelievers by your own statement.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the best of what has been said about its meaning is what Ibn Zayd said; he said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ — (ungrateful) for our favour, i.e. for the favour of my raising you.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿ قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذاً وَأَنَاْ مِنَ ٱلضَّالِّينَ﴾.
i.e. of the ignorant.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلضَّالِّينَ﴾ i.e. of the forgetful, as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿أَنْ تَضِلَّ إحْدَاهُمَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً﴾.
Al-Suddī said: It means prophethood.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
There are several statements on this verse:
a- It was said: the interrogative alif is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is that then a favour?"
As he said:
تَرُوْحُ منَ الحَيِّ أَمْ تَبْتكِرْ * وماذا يَضُرُّك لو تَنْتَظِرْ
(Will you leave the tribe in the evening or set out at dawn? And what harm would it do you if you waited?)
But this is not permissible, because if the alif is omitted from an interrogative, the meaning disappears, unless there is "أَمْ" or something similar in the speech.
And it was said: the meaning is: "And is that a favour you remind me of, that you enslaved me while I am of the Children of Israel?"
Because it is narrated that he raised him with the intention of enslaving him.
And it was said: "And is that a favour you remind me of, that you enslaved the Children of Israel and left me (free)?"
This is the best of the statements, because the wording indicates it; i.e. this only became a favour because you took the Children of Israel as slaves; had you not taken them as slaves, it would not have been a favour. So "أَنْ" is a badal (substitute) for "نعمة".
And it may be that the meaning is: because you enslaved the Children of Israel.

nahhas-meani:23-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Mūsā ﷺ answered him by informing him of the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which created beings are incapable of: ﴿قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ مُّوقِنِينَ﴾.
Pharaoh did not rebut this argument with anything more than saying: ﴿قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ أَلاَ تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾? i.e. do you not listen to his words?
So Mūsā answered him, because he was the one intended, and gave him more explanation.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
﴿قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَآئِكُمُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾. Pharaoh did not argue against him with anything more than attributing madness to him: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِيۤ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾.
i.e. one whose mind is overcome, because he says something that he (Pharaoh) does not recognise; for Pharaoh's people held that the one they knew as their lord at that time was "Pharaoh", and that those they knew as the lords of their forefathers of old were other kings who had been before Pharaoh.

nahhas-meani:28-30.t:
So Mūsā gave him more explanation and said ﴿رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Then Pharaoh threatened him: ﴿قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَـٰهَاً غَيْرِي لأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ﴾.
So Mūsā argued against him and against them with what they could witness: ﴿قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيءٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾? [verse 30].
i.e. with a decisive, clear proof that indicates my truthfulness.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
It is said: al-thuʿbān is the large serpent; and He said in another place ﴿تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ﴾.
And al-jānn is the small snake.
In this there is evidence that the sign was mighty, because He described its hugeness, and that it wriggled with the wriggling of a small one because of its lightness (agility), and its hugeness did not prevent it from that; and this is more tremendous as a sign.

nahhas-meani:33-36.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ﴾.
i.e. he drew his hand out of his bosom, and behold, it was white to the beholders, a luminous whiteness without leprosy.
Pharaoh rejected the mighty sign by attributing it to sorcery: ﴿قَالَ لِلْمَلإِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.
Then he humbled himself before them and said ﴿يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِّنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ؟ قَالُوۤاْ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِي ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَاشِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It means the police (al-shuraṭ).
It is narrated that the sorcerers were twelve thousand.
And that Mūsā was sent when sorcery was widespread, and he was given the mighty signs,
just as the Prophet ﷺ was sent when eloquence was at its peak, and he was given the Qurʾān, and they were challenged to produce a sūra like it, and they were unable to do that.
Qatāda said: ﴿إنَّهُ لَكَبيرُكُمْ﴾ means Mūsā ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ﴾.
It is narrated that he was the first to cut off (limbs) and to crucify.
﴿قَالُوا لاَ ضَيْرَ﴾ — in what befalls us of the punishment of this world, along with our hope for forgiveness.
One says: ضَرَرٌ, ضُرٌّ, ضَيْرٌ and ضَوْرٌ with one meaning (harm), and Abū ʿUbayda recited:
فإنَّكَ لا يَضُوْركَ بَعْدَ حَوْلٍ * أَظَبْيٌ كَانَ أمُّكَ أمْ حِمَارُ
(For it will not harm you, after a year, whether your mother was a gazelle or a donkey.)
﴿أَنْ كُنَّا أَوَّلَ المُؤْمِنينَ﴾ i.e. because we were.
Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. the first of the believers among the people of our time.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: This is the speech of one who does not know the narration, because it is narrated that there were with him six hundred and seventy thousand.
Rather the meaning is: the first to believe upon the appearance of this sign.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِيۤ﴾.
One says: سَرَى and أَسْرى when one travels by night.
Mujāhid said: Mūsā ﷺ went out by night.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: "They said to Pharaoh: Mūsā has gone out with the Children of Israel. He said: Do not speak to them until the cock crows. But no cock crowed that night. When morning came he had a sheep brought and slaughtered, and said: Its skinning will not be finished before five hundred thousand horsemen of the Copts are present. And they were present."
Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated from Abū Burda that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed with a Bedouin, who treated him generously. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: Keep in touch with us and come to us. So he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said to him: What do you need? He said: A she-camel to ride, and some goats for my family to milk. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Was this man incapable of being like the old woman of the Children of Israel? They said: And who was the old woman of the Children of Israel? He said: When Mūsā ﷺ wanted to go out with the Children of Israel, he lost the way, and said: What is this? The scholars of the Children of Israel said to him: When death came to Yūsuf, he took a covenant from us that we would not go out except with his bones. He said: Where is his grave? They said: No one knows it except the old woman of the Children of Israel. So they asked her, and she said: Not until you grant me my request. He said: And what is your request? She said: That I be with you in Paradise. He disliked that, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: Give it to her. So he did. She brought them to a small lake and said: Drain this water. So they drained it and brought out the bones of Yūsuf ﷺ, and the way became clear to them like the light of day.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِنَّكُم مّتَّبِعُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Pharaoh pursued him with a million stallions, besides the mares, while Mūsā, may Allah bless him, was with six hundred thousand of the Children of Israel. And Pharaoh said: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ لَشِرْذمةٌ قَلِيلُونَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ﴾ — he said: six hundred and seventy thousand.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad: ﴿وَإنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ﴾ — he said: equipped (muʾdūn).
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-muʾdūn are those who have equipment (adāt) with them, namely weapons; and weapons are the equipment of war.
And Abū ʿUbayda holds that "حَاذِرِينَ", "حَذِرينَ" and "حَذُرِينَ" — with ḍamma on the dhāl — have one meaning.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The reality of this is that al-ḥādhir is the one who makes ready, and al-ḥadhir is the one who is alert, as if that were in him by nature; and for this reason most of the grammarians said: "حَذِرٌ" is not transitive.
Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj narrated from Abū ʿAmmār that he read ﴿وَإنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَادِرُونَ﴾, with the dāl undotted. One says: جملٌ حَادِرٌ, when a camel is thick and full-bodied; and from it is the poet's saying:
وَعَيْنٌ لَهَا حَدْرَةٌ بَدْرَةٌ * شُقَّتْ مآقِيهمَا مِنْ أُخَر
(And an eye that is full and large, whose corners were slit from the back.)

nahhas-meani:57-58.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَاهُمْ مِّن جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ. وَكُنُوزٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [verses 57, 58].
Muḥammad ibn Salama al-Aswānī narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Sanjar narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us; he said: Ibn Lahīʿa narrated to us, from Wāhib ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, that "the Nile of Egypt" is the master of rivers: Allah subjected to it every river between the East and the West and made it submissive to it. When Allah wants to make the Nile of Egypt flow, He commands every river to supply it, so the rivers supply it with their water, and Allah makes springs gush forth for it from the earth. When its flow reaches what Allah wills, Allah reveals to every water to return to its source.
And he said about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَاهُمْ مِّن جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ. وَكُنُوزٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾:
He said: The gardens were on both banks of this Nile from its beginning to its end, on both sides together, from "Aswān" to "Rashīd" (Rosetta). And it had seven canals: "the canal of Alexandria", "the canal of Damietta", "the canal of Sardūs", "the canal of Manf (Memphis)", "the canal of al-Fayyūm" and "the canal of al-Manhā" [Translator's note: only six canals are named in the source], connected, none of them cut off from another; and the crops of all that lay between the two mountains, from the beginning of Egypt to its end, as far as the water reached. So all the land of Egypt was irrigated from (a flood of) sixteen cubits, through what they measured and arranged of its bridges, dams and canals.
He said: ﴿وَالمَقاَمُ الكَرِيمُ﴾ is the pulpits; there were a thousand pulpits in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-maqām in the language is the place, from your saying قامَ يقوم; and likewise al-maqāmāt, whose singular is maqāma, as the poet said:
وَفِيهِمْ مَقَاماتٌ حِسَانٌ وُجُوهُهَا * وَأَنْدِيَةٌ يَنْتَابُهَا القَوْلُ والفِعْلُ
(Among them are assemblies whose faces are handsome, and gatherings frequented by [wise] word and [noble] deed.)
And al-maqām is also the maṣdar (verbal noun); and al-muqām with ḍamma is the place, from أقام يُقيم, and also the maṣdar of أقامَ يُقيم. However, Ibn Lahīʿa said: I heard that "al-maqām al-karīm" is al-Fayyūm.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ﴾.
Most of the exegetes hold that the meaning is: at the time of sunrise.
Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is: toward the east.
The first is more fitting; one says: أشرقنا, i.e. we entered the sunrise, as one says: أصبحنا, i.e. we entered the morning; whereas for that (the direction) one only says: شرَّقنا and غرَّبنا (we went east, we went west).

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى ٱلْجَمْعَانِ﴾.
i.e. they saw one another.
﴿قَالَ أَصْحَابُ مُوسَىٰ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ﴾.
It has also been read ﴿لَمُدَّرَكُونَ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
i.e. this large host will overtake us, and we have no power against it.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ كَلاَّ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ﴾.
﴿كلاَّ﴾ i.e. desist and refrain from this statement:
﴿إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾ i.e. like the mountain, as al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said:
نَزَلُوا بأنْقِرَةٍ يَسيِلُ عَلَيْهِمُ * مَاءُ الفُرَاتِ يَجِيءُ منْ أَطْوَاد
(They alighted at Anqira, where the water of the Euphrates flows over them, coming down from the mountains [aṭwād].)
The plural of ṭawd, i.e. mountain.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ ٱلآخَرِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿أَزْلَفْنَا﴾: We destroyed.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿أزْلَفْنَا﴾: We gathered; and from it is the Night of al-Muzdalifa.
Qatāda said: ﴿أَزْلَفْنَا﴾: We brought them near to the sea and drowned them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These statements are close to one another, because He only gathered them for destruction; and Qatāda's statement is the soundest of them. From it is ﴿وأُزْلِفَتِ الجنَّةُ للمتَّقِين﴾, and:
"مرَّ اللَّيالي زُلَفاً فَزُلَفَاً"
(the passing of the nights, stage by stage drawing near)
It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read "وأزلقنا" with qāf.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.
i.e. the news of Ibrāhīm.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَاماً فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَاكِفِينَ﴾.
i.e. persisting in their worship.
﴿قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ﴾?
Abū ʿUbayda said: i.e. do they listen to you?
Abū Ḥātim said: i.e. do they hear your voices?
Qatāda read ﴿هل يُسْمِعُونَكُمْ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. do they make you hear their voices and their speech?

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِيۤ إِلاَّ رَبَّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
It may be an exception not from the first (i.e. a disjoined exception).
And it may be that the meaning is: everything you worship is an enemy to me on the Day of Resurrection, except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Among the soundest of what has been said about it is that the meaning is: for they would be an enemy to me on the Day of Resurrection, were I to worship them.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿فَهُوَ يَهْدِيِني﴾ with the yāʾ retained in all of them.
And he read ﴿وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطَايَايَ يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ (my sins, plural).
And he said: It is not a single sin.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The singular is good, with خطيئة having the meaning of خَطَايا, as was read ﴿وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَةً ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said about His saying ﴿والَّذِي أَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لي خَطِيئَتي﴾:
He said: It is his saying ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيُرهُم هَذَا﴾ and his saying ﴿إنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾,
and his saying, when one of the pharaohs wanted to take "Sāra": She is my sister.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
Mujāhid said about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَٱجْعَل لِّي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾:
He said: good praise.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the agreement of the nations upon him.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: i.e. sound (free) from polytheism.
ʿUrwa said: He never cursed anything at all.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
i.e. it was brought near, meaning: their entering it drew near.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكُبْكِبُواْ فِيهَا هُمْ وَٱلْغَاوُونَ﴾.
"كُبْكِبُوا" i.e. they were turned over on their heads.
And it was said: some of them were thrown on top of others; this is the statement of Abū ʿUbayda.
The origin is كُبِّبُوا; then a kāf was substituted for the (second) bāʾ, because the doubling was found heavy.
And it was said: the meaning of ﴿فَكُبْكِبُواْ﴾ is: they were gathered together, derived from كَوْكَب of a thing, i.e. its bulk; and a body of horsemen is called kawkab and kabkaba.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَٱلْغَاوُونَ﴾ are the devils.
Al-Suddī said: ﴿فَكُبْكِبُواْ﴾ i.e. the polytheists of the Arabs; ﴿الْغَاوُونَ﴾: the gods; and ﴿جُنُوْدُ إِبْلِيسَ﴾: those who were of his offspring.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ is: we worship you as we worship Him.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَافِعِينَ. وَلاَ صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ﴾.
﴿حَمِيمٍ﴾ i.e. close (intimate); and from it is ḥāmmat al-rajul (a man's close kin). The origin of this is from al-ḥamīm, which is hot water; and from it come al-ḥammām (the bath) and al-ḥummā (fever).
So a man's ḥāmma are those whom what burns him burns, as one says: هم حُزَانتُهم, i.e. what grieves him grieves them.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
Yaʿqūb and others read ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَأَتْبَاعُكَ ٱلأَرْذَلُونَ﴾.
It is a good reading. This wāw is most often followed by nouns, with verbs coming afterwards. ﴿أَتْبَاعُ﴾ is the plural of tabaʿ, and tabaʿ is used for the singular and the plural. The poet said:
لَهُ تَبَعٌ قَدْ يَعْلَم النَّاسُ أنَّه * عَلَى مَنْ تَدَانى صَيِّفٌ وَرَبِيع
(He has a following [tabaʿ], and people know that he is, to those who draw near, a summer rain and a spring rain.)
And it was said: They only meant that your followers are the cuppers and the weavers.
But crafts are not harmful in religion.
ʿĪsā ibn Maymūn narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, and Saʿīd (narrated) from Qatāda: ﴿وَاتَّبَعَكَ الأَرْذَلُونَ﴾ — he said: the weavers.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأَنجَيْنَاهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ﴾.
Al-mashḥūn is the filled (laden).

nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ﴾.
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-rīʿ is the road.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ﴾ — on every mountain pass (fajj).
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-fajj is the road in the mountain.
A number of the lexicographers said: al-rīʿ is what is elevated of the ground, the plural of rīʿa; and كم رَيْعُ أرضك؟ i.e. how high is your land?
It is well known in the language that what is elevated of the ground is called "رَيْعٌ" and the road "رِيعٌ", and Allah knows best what He meant.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبُثْونَ﴾ —
he said: pigeon towers.

nahhas-meani:129-129.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿مَصَانِعَ﴾ — he said: palaces and fortresses.
Sufyān said: They are water reservoirs.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: Its singular is maṣnaʿ and maṣnaʿa.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What Mujāhid said, that al-maṣāniʿ are palaces and fortresses, is well known in the language.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Every building is called maṣnaʿ and maṣnaʿa.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ﴾ — he said: with baked brick and clay.
In one of the readings: ﴿كأَنكمْ تَخْلُدُونَ﴾ (as though you will live forever); and the two meanings are close, because the meaning of ﴿لَعلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ﴾ is that you are in hope of immortality.

nahhas-meani:130-130.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا بَطَشْتُمْ بَطَشْتُمْ جَبَّارِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: with the sword and the whip.

nahhas-meani:137-137.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ هَـٰذَا إِلاَّ خُلُقُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿خُلُقُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾ with ḍamma: they live as they (the ancients) lived, i.e. we live and die as they lived and died.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: ﴿خُلْقُ الأَوَّلينَ﴾ [Translator's note: the source prints this with sukūn; ʿAbd Allāh's reading is normally given as خَلْقُ] i.e. their fabrication.
Abū Jaʿfar said: خَلَق الشَّيْءَ and اختلَقَه have one meaning (he fabricated the thing).

nahhas-meani:148-148.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَزُرُوعٍ وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. some of it piled on top of other.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it was said: ﴿هَضِيمٌ﴾ i.e. digestible and wholesome,
delicate when it first comes out.
Mujāhid said: When it comes out, one grips it and it crumbles (yahḍimuhu).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of al-haḍm is the drawing together of a thing; and from it:
* "هَضِيمُ الكَشْحِ رَيَّا المُخَلْخَلِ" *
(slender of waist, full where the anklet sits)
And from it: فلانٌ أهضمُ الكَشْحِ, i.e. lean-waisted. So the spathe is called haḍīm before it opens.
Isḥāq narrated from Burayd: ﴿وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌ﴾ —
he said: some of it has already ripened into fresh dates, and some is ripening from the tip (mudhannab).

nahhas-meani:149-149.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً فَارِهِينَ﴾.
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: i.e. skilled in carving them.
Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir said: ﴿فَارِهين﴾ i.e. skilled.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿فَرِهِينَ﴾ i.e. secure.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād said: ﴿فَارِهيِنَ﴾, with alif, i.e. tyrannical.
Qatāda said: ﴿فَرِهين﴾ i.e. self-admiring.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَرِهينَ﴾ i.e. insolent and exultant.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best known of them in the language, and it is the statement of Abū ʿAmr and Abū ʿUbayda; it is as if the hāʾ were substituted for a ḥāʾ [i.e. فَرِحين], because they are both guttural letters.
And Abū ʿUbayda holds that ﴿فَارِهِينَ﴾ and ﴿فَرِهِينَ﴾ have one meaning.

nahhas-meani:153-153.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ﴾.
i.e. of the bewitched; Mujāhid said this.
Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is: you are only a human being who has a saḥr, and al-saḥr is the lung.
And it was said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ﴾ i.e. of those who are nourished (diverted) with food and drink, as the poet said:
أُرَانا مُوْضِعِينَ لَحَتْمِ غَيْبٍ * وَنُسْحَرُ بالطَّعَامِ وَبِالشَّرَابِ
(I see us hastening toward an unseen decree, while we are beguiled with food and drink.)

nahhas-meani:155-155.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ﴾.
Al-shirb is the share of water.

nahhas-meani:166-166.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِّنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ﴾.
Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir said: Mujāhid said to me: How does ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ﴾? I said: "وَتَذَرُونَ ما أَصْلَحَ ربُّكُمْ منْ أزواجكُم" (and you leave what your Lord has made fit for you of your wives). He said: The vulva, as He, the Exalted, said ﴿فَأْتُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ أمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِّنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ﴾ —
he said: (you leave) the front, the vulva, (turning) to the backsides of women and men.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ﴾.
One says: عَدَا when one exceeds the bounds in wrongdoing.

nahhas-meani:168-168.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْقَالِينَ﴾.
i.e. of those who hate and detest. One says: قَلاَه يَقْليه, qilan and qalāʾan (he hated him), as he said:
عَلَيْكِ السَّلامُ لا مُلِلْتِ قَرِيبَةً * ومَالَكِ عنْدِي إنْ نَأَيْتَ قَلاَءُ
(Peace be upon you; may you not be found tiresome when near, and you meet no hatred from me if you go far away.)

nahhas-meani:171-171.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ عَجُوزاً فِي ٱلْغَابِرِينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. of those who remained.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The one who departs is called ghābir, and the one who remains is called ghābir, as he said:
لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْل بأَغْبارِها * إنَّك لا تَدْرِي مَنِ النَّاتِجُ
(Do not splash cold water on the udders of the dry she-camels while they still have their remaining milk, for you do not know who will deliver their young.)
And as he said:
فَمَا وَنَى محمَّدٌ مُذْ أَنْ غَفَر * لَهُ الإلَهُ ما مَضَى ومَا غَبَر
(Muḥammad has not slackened since God forgave him what had passed and what remained.)
i.e. and what remained.
Al-aghbār are the remnants of milk, and al-shawl are the camels that have raised their tails.

nahhas-meani:176-176.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.
Al-ayka according to the lexicographers is dense, intertwined trees, and the plural is ayk. It is narrated that they were people of dense, intertwined trees.
It has been said that al-Ayka is the name of a place, but that is not sound and is not known.

nahhas-meani:177-177.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلاَ تَتَّقُونَ﴾.
It was read to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Muḥammad, who said: Makhlad narrated to us; he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: All the prophets are from the Children of Israel except ten: "Nūḥ, Ṣāliḥ, Hūd, Shuʿayb, Ibrāhīm, Lūṭ, Ismāʿīl, Isḥāq, Yaʿqūb and Muḥammad", may Allah bless them.
Al-Sharqī ibn Quṭāmī claimed that Shuʿayb was the son of ʿAyfā ibn Nuwayb ibn Madyan ibn Ibrāhīm.
And Ibn Samʿān claimed that Shuʿayb was the son of Jazī ibn Yashjur ibn Lāwī ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, may Allah bless them. [Translator's note: the source spells the name ولاوي, i.e. "wa-Lāwī".]

nahhas-meani:182-182.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَزِنُواْ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said: ﴿القِسْطَاسُ﴾ is justice.

nahhas-meani:183-183.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَبْخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ﴾.
i.e. and do not wrong (them); and from it is the Arabs' saying: "تحسبُها حَمْقَاءَ وهيَ بَاخِسُ" (You think her foolish, while she is cheating [you]).

nahhas-meani:184-184.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿الجِبِلَّةُ﴾ is creation (the created beings).
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says: جُبِلَ فلانٌ على كَذَا, i.e. he was created (with such a nature).
And His saying (may be read) ﴿جِبِلَّةٌ﴾, ﴿جُبُلَّةٌ﴾ and ﴿جُبْلَةٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:187-187.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفاً﴾ — he said: a side (portion).
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is (also) read ﴿كِسَفاً﴾, which is the plural of kisfa, which is the piece. [Translator's note: the two spellings are identical in the source; the variants usually distinguished are كِسْفاً and كِسَفاً.]

nahhas-meani:189-189.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: Intense heat struck them, so they entered the houses, and it seized their breath; so they went out into the open country where nothing shaded them. Then Allah sent a cloud to them, and they fled to it to take shade under it, and called to one another. When they had gathered beneath it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them.
Mujāhid said: When they had gathered beneath it, a shout was cried at them and they perished.

nahhas-meani:193-193.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلأَمِينُ﴾.
Meaning Jibrīl, may Allah bless him.
﴿عَلَى قَلْبِكَ﴾ i.e. he recites it, and your heart retains it.

nahhas-meani:196-196.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَفِي زُبُرِ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
i.e. its being sent down and its mention (are in the scriptures of the ancients).

nahhas-meani:197-197.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أَوَ لَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ آيَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَمَاءُ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿أو ليسَ لكم آيةً أَنْ يعلمَهُ عُلماءُ بني إسْرائيلَ﴾?
Mujāhid said: It is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
Someone else said: It is ʿAbd Allāh and others of those who embraced Islam.

nahhas-meani:198-198.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَاهُ عَلَىٰ بَعْضِ ٱلأَعْجَمِينَ﴾.
Al-aʿjam is the one who does not speak clearly, even if he is an Arab.
And al-ʿajamī is the one whose origin is from the non-Arabs, even if he is eloquent.
We have mentioned His saying ﴿كَذَلِكَ سَلَكْنَاهُ في قُلُوبِ المُجْرِمينَ﴾ in Sūrat al-Ḥajj. [Translator's note: the phrase كذلك سلكناه في قلوب المجرمين occurs at 26:200; a similar phrase, كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين, is at 15:12 (Sūrat al-Ḥijr). "al-Ḥajj" may be a slip for "al-Ḥijr".]

nahhas-meani:212-212.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ﴾.
i.e. they are prevented from listening to the revelation by being pelted (with meteors).
ʿUrwa narrated from ʿĀʾisha, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, the soothsayers used to tell us something, and we would find it as they said? He said: That is the word one of them snatches, and he tells [a hundred lies] along with it." And he mentioned the ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:214-214.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ ٱلأَقْرَبِينَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed al-Ṣafā and cried out: "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" (an alarm call). So they gathered to him, some men coming and some sending a messenger. He said: Do you see, if I told you that a man had come from this mountain pass to raid you, would you believe me? [They said: Yes, we have found nothing in you but truthfulness. He said:] Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.
Abū Lahab said: Is it for this that you summoned us? Perish you! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبي لَهَبٍ وتبَّ﴾.
Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "O Ṣafiyya, aunt of the Messenger of Allah; O Fāṭima, daughter of Muḥammad; O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me of my wealth whatever you wish."

nahhas-meani:218-219.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِي يَرَاكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ. وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِي ٱلسَّاجِدِينَ﴾ [verses 218–219].
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿في السَّاجِدين﴾ — among those who pray.
Mujāhid said: And he used to see those behind him as he saw those in front of him.
ʿIkrima said: i.e. standing, bowing and prostrating.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: His passing through the loins (of his forefathers) until He brought him forth as a prophet.

nahhas-meani:222-222.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنَزَّلُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿عَلَىٰ كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ﴾ — upon every liar.

nahhas-meani:224-224.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ ٱلْغَاوُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: (They are) the transmitters (of poetry).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They were two men who satirised each other in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one of them from the Anṣār; with each of them was a group, and they are the misguided fools.
ʿIkrima said: They are those who follow the poet.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الغَاوُونَ﴾ — he said: the devils.
Khuṣayf narrated from Mujāhid, who said: They are those who follow them and transmit their poetry.

nahhas-meani:225-225.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. they range through every art (genre).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied form in the language is: in every valley of speech they wander.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-hāʾim is the one who departs from the right course in everything.

nahhas-meani:227-227.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: It means ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa and Ḥassān.
In another ḥadīth than this: when this verse was revealed, ʿAbd Allāh said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that we compose poetry, and He has revealed this? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ، وَذَكَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيراً وَٱنتَصَرُواْ مِن بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ﴾, i.e. they defended the Prophet ﷺ and the believers against those who satirised them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمْ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوۤاْ أَيَّ مُنقَلَبٍ يَنقَلِبُونَ﴾ [verse 227].
It is narrated in the ḥadīth that He meant by it (a return) from before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the Fire.
